reader.requirement: At --std 85, when an FD of a sequential (or report) file specifies CODE-SET IS alphabet-name-1 (STANDARD-1, STANDARD-2, NATIVE or an implementor-name; never a literal-phrase alphabet), from a successful OPEN the medium holds the data in that alphabet's character set, and every input and output operation (READ, WRITE, REWRITE, EXTEND, report lines) converts each record character between the medium set and the native set through the alphabet's correspondence.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses the 2002 national phrases (alphabet-name-2, FOR ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL) below 2002 via Constructs.CodeSetNational2002 (COBOL0900)

reader.notes: The conversion is applied at the one physical framing boundary on every output and input path probed, organization-independent and edition-free. Doubt stated: HIGH-VALUE (native U+FFFF) is written as the set's highest code unit, so the native character the alphabet assigns that unit (U+009F under EBCDIC, DEL under STANDARD-1) reads back as HIGH-VALUE (cs02: E2 NOT X9F); this is the owner's decision kb/Work R51 item 4, documented in docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-187.md, and HIGH-VALUE's correspondent is unstated by 1985, so it is not counted as a divergence here. The COBOL2604 message cites §2023 rules at --std 85.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the input/output operations the reader did not try, at --std 85 under refute-1985-120/: cssort.cob SORT USING a CODE-SET EBCDIC file GIVING a CODE-SET EBCDIC file, then MERGE USING it and a second EBCDIC file GIVING a third: records sorted BB02 aa01 dd04 and merged BB02 CC03 ZZ09 aa01 dd04, raw medium of both outputs 194 194 240 242 (EBCDIC 'BB02'), so SORT/MERGE I-O converts both ways; csrev.cob OPEN OUTPUT WITH NO REWIND, CLOSE WITH NO REWIND (07), OPEN INPUT REVERSED (a 1985-only obsolete form): REV cd2 / REV AB1 converted back; cssame.cob SAME RECORD AREA with a non-CODE-SET file sees the converted native record (SHARED Ab1$), and a contained program's FD using the containing program's alphabet converts (INNER Ab1$, raw 193); csstd2.cob STANDARD-2 round trips $~a@ with medium 36 126 97 64 (the IRV correspondence is implementor territory per §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4a); csadv.cob WRITE ADVANCING and LINAGE files under EBCDIC: record characters including interior and trailing spaces are EBCDIC (c1 40 c2 40 40 40; d7 40 d8 40 40 40), only the line-control bytes (0a, 0c, 0d 0a) are native, which is device framing, not data; cslit.cob a literal-phrase alphabet is refused (COBOL1672) and cscomp.cob COMP and unseparated sign refused (COBOL1672, SR1). Edition sites: grep of src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/IO for DialectLevel/Edition found only RelativeConnector, IndexedConnector, ReportWriter, FileRegistry sharing/lock arms, none in the code-set path; VersionConformancePass#VisitCodeSetClause confirmed. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.3.4.4 GR1b  (3.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1b'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.4.3 SR1  (3.4.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1'; 'OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4a  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4a'. Leads outside this rule: COBOL1672 and COBOL2604 cite only §2023 rules at --std 85, and the literal-alphabet refusal is worded as an implementor non-support rather than §1985:VII.3.4.3 SR2.
